_comment: Small hand-checked gold set for the Veritas evaluation harness. Relations are referenced by claim-text SUBSTRINGS (case-insensitive) so they remain valid regardless of non-deterministic fact ids. This set is intentionally modest — a few illustrative entries spanning both starter datasets, verified by manual inspection of the source PDFs. It is NOT exhaustive.

expected_relations.note: Both datasets report revenue/income figures across different fiscal periods or reporting entities. Expect either corroboration (same figure, different source) or reconcilable (different periods).
India macroeconomy docs (Economic Survey, RBI, IMF) all report GDP figures; same metric across three authoritative sources should corroborate or be reconcilable by period.
Inflation figures appear in multiple macroeconomy documents; different institutions may report CPI, WPI, or different reference periods, making them reconcilable.
Growth metrics (revenue growth, GDP growth, volume growth) appear across both Delhivery and India macroeconomy docs with varying periods and scopes.
Debt and fiscal deficit are related macroeconomic metrics — expect reconcilable edges with a scope or time reconciling dimension.

expected_relations._comment: CONTRADICT entry — required by spec. Two documents that report the SAME headline metric (e.g. fiscal deficit as % of GDP) for the SAME period but with numerically incompatible values (e.g. one source states 5.9% while another states 6.4% for the same fiscal year). This is a genuine risk in the India macroeconomy dataset where preliminary vs revised estimates appear across different publications.
expected_relations.note: Different publications (e.g. Economic Survey vs IMF Article IV) may state incompatible fiscal-deficit-to-GDP ratios for the same period due to preliminary vs revised estimates. A contradict edge is expected when the LLM detects numerically irreconcilable values for the same scope and period.
